morphology.formula: bernafas + -lah → bernafaslah；底层构词：ber- + nafas → bernafas
morphology.pattern_note: -lah 是附着于词尾的强调语助词，不是派生后缀；添加时词干不变。root_word 保留数据包的直接基础词 bernafas，进一步词根为 nafas。所给 Jawi 对应 bernafas，未包含 -lah。

senses.zh_definition: 呼吸；带 -lah 时，通常表示劝告、指示或强调“呼吸吧”。
senses.en_definition: To breathe; with -lah, commonly an instruction or encouragement to breathe.
senses.nuances: -lah 不改变 bernafas 的基本词义；语气取决于语调，可温和劝导，也可加强指示。[DBP：bernafas](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=206468&keyword=bernafas)

senses.en_definition: To be alive; to have life.
senses.nuances: 这是基础词 bernafas 的引申义，常见于文学、感慨或生命主题表达。完整形式 bernafaslah 用于此义时，多带劝勉或诗性语气。

collocations.en: as long as one is still alive

senses.zh_definition: 具有某种思想、精神或文化色彩。
senses.en_definition: To be imbued with a particular spirit, influence, or character.
senses.nuances: 属于文学及评论用语，通常以基础词 bernafas 修饰作品。完整形式 bernafaslah 在此义下较少见，不宜为了套用目标词而强造日常句子。

collocations.zh: 具有伊斯兰精神的诗歌
collocations.en: poetry imbued with an Islamic spirit

dual_scenarios.context: 公文 / 新闻 / 职场汇报
dual_scenarios.ms: Dalam sesi latihan pengucapan awam, fasilitator memberikan arahan, “Bernafaslah seperti biasa sebelum memulakan ucapan.”
dual_scenarios.zh: 在公众演讲培训中，培训员指示：“开始讲话前，请保持正常呼吸。”
dual_scenarios.en: During the public speaking workshop, the facilitator instructed participants, “Breathe normally before beginning your speech.”

dual_scenarios.ms_spoken: Bernafaslah dulu, jangan gelabah sangat. Kau dah berlatih banyak kali.
dual_scenarios.ms_standard: Bernafaslah dahulu dan jangan terlalu cemas. Kamu sudah berlatih banyak kali.
dual_scenarios.zh: 先缓口气，别那么紧张。你都练过很多遍了。
dual_scenarios.en: Take a breath first. Don't get so nervous—you've practised plenty of times.
spoken_features: dulu 是 dahulu 的常用口语形式
很口语的 gelabah sangat 表示特别慌张

messages.speaker: Amir (朋友)
messages.ms_spoken: Aku dah sampai kat dewan, tapi gelabah pula nak naik pentas.
messages.ms_standard: Saya sudah tiba di dewan, tetapi saya berasa cemas untuk naik ke pentas.
messages.zh: 我已经到礼堂了，可是一想到上台就紧张。
messages.en: I'm at the hall already, but now I'm nervous about going on stage.

messages.speaker: Farah (朋友)
messages.ms_spoken: Bernafaslah dulu. Kau dah berlatih banyak kali, kan?
messages.ms_standard: Bernafaslah dahulu. Kamu sudah berlatih banyak kali, bukan?
messages.zh: 先缓口气。你不是已经练过很多遍了吗？
messages.en: Take a breath first. You've practised plenty of times, haven't you?

etymology.historical_story: Nafas comes from Arabic nafas, meaning breath, a connection shared with Turkish nefes. Malay gives this borrowed noun its own grammatical clothing: ber- forms the verb bernafas, and -lah adds emphasis or encouragement. The resulting word shows how an imported everyday concept can become fully integrated into Malay word formation and conversational expression. [Etymological study](https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/aiugr/9/0/9_51/_pdf/-char/ja)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把 nafas 记成“一口气”：ber- 让它成为呼吸动作，-lah 像轻声加一句“吧”——bernafaslah，呼吸吧。

cultural_pragmatics.politeness_note: -lah 本身不保证礼貌。柔和语调可表达安慰，急促或不耐烦的语调则可能像命令；面对不熟悉的人可说“Cuba bernafas perlahan-lahan”。
cultural_pragmatics.usage_etiquette: 适合演讲训练、运动指导及熟人间安抚情绪。对方认真倾诉时，单独丢一句 bernafaslah 可能显得敷衍，宜配合倾听和具体回应。
